name: Beechcraft Queen Air
summary: Large nine-seat Beechcraft twin built 1960–1978 from the Twin Bonanza, the airframe that evolved into the King Air.

wings: Low, straight wing with deep engine nacelles
engines: Two big six-cylinder piston engines in nacelles with no exhaust stacks
fuselage: Long, deep cabin with a row of rounded-square windows
tail: Early models: tall, upright, squared-off fin
Later models: swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Looks like a King Air but with piston cowlings and no exhaust stacks
Long, deep cabin with a row of rounded-square windows
Upright squared fin (early) or swept fin with dorsal fillet (later)

confusedWith.howToTell: The King Air has turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks; the Queen Air has plain piston cowlings.
The Twin Bonanza is much shorter with a smaller cabin; the Queen Air has a long, deep fuselage.
The Aero Commander has a high wing; the Queen Air has a low wing.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
